dataset.description:
This dataset contains experimental, analytical, biological, formulation, and market-relevant data generated within the POLYCLAY-UV project, which develops clay–polyphenol composite materials derived from spent coffee grounds and tea leaves for use as natural-origin UV filters in cosmetic formulations. The data support the development and validation of sustainable UV-protective cosmetic ingredients up to technology readiness level (TRL) 4.
The dataset includes raw laboratory data from composite synthesis and sorption studies; physicochemical and structural characterisation data obtained using FTIR, TGA, SEM/EDS, XRD, and LC-MS; formulation compatibility and stability data; and in vitro safety and efficacy results, including UV absorption, SPF estimation, cytotoxicity, phototoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and extracellular matrix-related biomarkers in skin cell models. In addition, anonymised qualitative data from interviews and workshops with cosmetic formulators and industry stakeholders are included to support market validation and commercialisation planning.

distribution.title:
The purpose of the data collection is to generate scientific and technological evidence supporting the development of natural-origin UV filters for cosmetic applications based on clay–polyphenol composite materials derived from spent coffee grounds and tea leaves. The collected data enable optimisation of composite synthesis, evaluation of physicochemical stability and formulation compatibility, and assessment of UV-protective performance, biological safety, and skin-relevant bioactivity, directly supporting the project’s objectives to advance the technology from TRL 2 to TRL 4.
The data originate from primary experimental work conducted within the project, including laboratory-based synthesis and characterisation of clay–polyphenol composites, in vitro safety and efficacy testing using skin cell models, formulation stability assessments, and market-oriented data collection through interviews and workshops with cosmetic formulators and industry stakeholders. Together, these data provide a coherent basis for validating the functionality, safety, and application potential of the developed materials and for informing future regulatory preparation and scale-up activities.

dataset.title: Dataset of the POLYCLAY-UV Project: Experimental, Analytical and In Vitro Data on Clay–Polyphenol Composite Materials for Natural UV Filters in Cosmetics

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) describes the management of data generated within the POLYCLAY-UV project, which aims to develop multifunctional clay–polyphenol composite materials derived from spent coffee grounds and tea leaves for use as natural-origin UV filters in cosmetic formulations. The DMP provides an overview of the types of data collected, their intended use, and the procedures applied to ensure data quality, integrity, security, and compliance with Open Science and FAIR data principles.

The project encompasses interdisciplinary research activities, including material synthesis and optimisation, physicochemical and structural characterisation, formulation compatibility testing, in vitro biological safety and efficacy assessment, technology validation, and market and regulatory analysis. As a result, diverse datasets are generated throughout laboratory experiments, analytical measurements, cell-based assays, formulation testing, stakeholder engagement activities, and project documentation.

The DMP covers the following main categories of data: raw experimental data from composite synthesis and sorption studies; analytical datasets obtained using FTIR, TGA, SEM/EDS, XRD, LC-MS and related techniques; cosmetic formulation stability and compatibility data; in vitro bioactivity and safety testing results related to UV protection performance; anonymised market and stakeholder data collected through interviews and workshops; and project-related documentation such as protocols, standard operating procedures, calibration records, reports, and evidence of technology readiness level (TRL) progression.

The purpose of this DMP is to ensure that all data generated within the project are handled in a structured and transparent manner, remain reusable and traceable throughout the project lifecycle, and can be appropriately shared, archived, or preserved beyond the project duration, in line with ethical, legal, and regulatory requirements.
dmp.ethical_issues_description: Legal considerations relate primarily to intellectual property protection and commercial sensitivity. These factors may affect the timing and conditions of data sharing but do not prevent data collection within the project.
